intro.headline: Where is your sales system leaking?
intro.sub: 23 questions. About 6 minutes. You get a score across nine parts of your sales system, your top three leaks, the math on your own numbers, and fixes you can run this week.

numbers_intro: Now the numbers. Rough is fine. Pick "I don't know" if you don't.

config._note: Every value here is a DEFAULT, not an industry statistic. Dylan to confirm each one.
config.display_rounding: counts to whole numbers, except sales (closes), which show 1 decimal; rates and per-day figures to 1 decimal; money to whole dollars, and money of 1,000 or more to the nearest 100. Math runs on unrounded values.

categories.name: Hiring system
categories.good: There's a vetted bench before anyone quits. Every candidate roleplays your offer before an offer letter.

leak.title: Hiring starts when someone quits
leak.why: Every gap between closers is a month of leads worked by whoever's left. Usually you.
fixes: Keep one job post live all the time. Interview two people a week, even when you're full.
Make every candidate roleplay your actual offer for 15 minutes.
Write the three things your best closer does that your last bad hire didn't. Hire for those.
leak.cta_line: The Hiring App keeps a vetted bench, so the next closer is already waiting.

categories.name: Onboarding and ramp
categories.good: New reps study real calls, roleplay daily, and certify before live leads. First close inside a few weeks.

leak.title: New reps take too long to pay for themselves
leak.looks_like: First close for a new closer: {rp_first}. Day one gets them: {rp_day1}.
leak.why: A rep who takes three months to ramp burns three months of leads at a lower close rate.
fixes: Pick your 10 best recorded calls. That's week one.
Certify before live leads: they pitch you the offer and handle your top three objections.
Fifteen-minute roleplay every day for a new rep's first two weeks.
leak.cta_line: Closer Onboarding gives every new rep the same first two weeks, without you running it.

categories.name: Speed to lead
categories.good: Every new lead gets a call inside 5 minutes, and time-to-first-call is reported by rep.

leak.title: Speed to lead depends on who's free
leak.why: The lead was most interested the minute they opted in. Every hour after that, someone else's ad is in their feed.
fixes: Instant text and a call task the second a lead comes in.
Report time-to-first-call by rep every morning.
Set a five-day call and text cadence for leads who don't pick up.
leak.cta_line: Speed to Lead routes and timestamps every new lead, so nothing sits.

categories.name: Call QC and coaching
categories.good: Every call gets scored against one written scorecard. Reps see their scores every week.

leak.title: Nobody knows what happens on the calls
leak.looks_like_numbers: Calls reviewed: {qc_share}. {close_pct}% of held calls close. Each 5 points of close rate is worth about ${close5} a month.
leak.why: Close rate gets made on the calls. If nobody's listening, the same objection loses the same deal every week.
fixes: Write a 10-line scorecard. Every review uses it.
Score two calls per rep this week. Share the scores with the team.
Pull three lost calls. Find the minute the prospect checked out.
leak.cta_line: AI Call Coaching scores every call against your scorecard, not just the ones someone had time for.

categories.name: Manager cadence and EOD
categories.good: A manager runs the daily huddle and weekly one-on-ones. EODs come in structured and get a reply.

leak.title: The team runs on someone's evenings
leak.looks_like: Day to day, the team is managed by: {cd_who}. EOD reports: {cd_eod}.
leak.why: If the cadence depends on one person's free time, it stops the week that person gets busy.
fixes: Three numbers and one question in every EOD. Reply to each by 9 a.m.
Fifteen-minute huddle every morning: yesterday's numbers, today's calls, one skill.
Weekly one-on-one with each rep: their numbers, one call clip, one goal.
leak.cta_line: Manager OS runs the EOD, huddle, and one-on-one rhythm so it doesn't live in one head.

categories.name: Setter and closer tracking
categories.part: Phone & DM Setter Trackers, QC Dashboard
categories.good: Every rep's booked, showed, closed, and collected is visible today. Show rate is split by who booked it.

leak.title: You see team totals, not reps
leak.looks_like: Numbers by rep: {tr_rep}. Show rate split: {tr_split}. Core numbers you didn't know: {unknown_count} of 4.
leak.looks_like_numbers: You booked {booked} and {show_pct}% showed. Each 5 points of show rate is worth about ${show5} a month. Numbers by rep: {tr_rep}. Show rate split: {tr_split}.
leak.why: A blended number hides the rep dragging it down and the setter carrying it.
fixes: One sheet, one row per rep: booked, showed, closed, collected. Updated daily.
Tag every booking setter or self. Compare show rates next Friday.
Review cash per booked call every Monday.
leak.cta_line: The Setter Trackers and QC Dashboard show every rep's numbers live.

categories.name: Commission and pay
categories.good: Commission is calculated from collected cash, automatically, with a written clawback rule.

leak.title: Commission is a monthly argument
leak.why: Paying on closed means paying on deals that never collect. Hand math means disputes, and disputes cost you good reps.
fixes: Reconcile last month's commissions against Stripe before the next payout.
Pay on collected cash. Write the clawback rule down.
Send each rep a statement: deals, cash collected, commission. Same format every time.
leak.cta_line: The Commission Tracker pays from collected cash, automatically.

categories.name: CRM and data trust
categories.good: CRM, Stripe, and the manager's numbers agree to the dollar. Every call outcome is logged the same day.

leak.title: Three systems, three numbers
leak.looks_like: CRM vs Stripe vs manager: {dt_agree}. Call outcomes logged: {dt_log}.
leak.why: If the numbers don't agree, every meeting is about whose number is right instead of what to fix.
fixes: Put last month's CRM cash and Stripe cash side by side. Find the gap.
No commission until the call outcome is logged.
Pick one source of truth for cash and tell the team which one.
leak.cta_line: RevPhlo ties GHL, Stripe, and Fathom together so there's one number.

categories.name: Playbooks
categories.good: Scripts and objection handling are written, dated, and updated from real calls.

leak.title: The playbook lives in someone's head
leak.why: If it isn't written down, every rep runs a different pitch and nobody can coach to a standard.
fixes: Transcribe your top rep's best call. That's version one.
List your top five objections and the answer that works. One page.
Date the script. Review it every month.
leak.cta_line: The Closer and Setter Playbooks come written, then get tuned to your calls.

archetypes.means: You have a manager. The data underneath isn't strong enough to manage with.

grade_bands.line: Tight. The leaks are small. Protect what works.
Solid, with a couple of real leaks.
You're selling in spite of the system.

The pipeline is a sieve. Fix the top leak first.

scoring.category_score: round(mean(item scores in category) / 4 * 100). Items = answered choice questions in the category + number questions with score_bands in the category (unknown = skipped there) + known/unknown items routed via known_scores_category (known = 4, unknown = 0). Categories with no items are left out.
scoring.rounding: round() is round half up (12.5 -> 13), same as JavaScript Math.round for positive numbers. Not banker's rounding.
scoring.grade: first grade band where overall_score >= min
scoring.archetype: sum option points per archetype; highest total wins; ties broken by archetype_tiebreak order; all zero = first in tiebreak order
scoring.leaks: one leak per category. A category is a leak if its score < config.leak_threshold. Rank leaks by category score ascending; ties broken by category order. Show the top 3. If fewer than 3 qualify, show only those.
scoring.looks_like: Use looks_like_numbers if every {token} in it resolves, else looks_like. Choice tokens {question_id} resolve to the chosen option label. Math tokens resolve from math outputs.
scoring.quick_wins: For every answered choice option with score <= 1, take that question's quick_win. Order by category score ascending, then question order. Cap at config.max_quick_wins.

results_copy.heading: Your sales system diagnostic
results_copy.math_note: Only your inputs. Rounded. Nothing here is a forecast.
results_copy.no_leaks: Nothing scored under the leak line. The work is keeping it there.
results_copy.no_math: You skipped the numbers, so there's no math. That's a finding too.
